turns.content: It's 2am and I'm still at the office. Not working — just sitting. The bridge round officially died on Tuesday. Rohit and Sneha put in their papers this week, which honestly, smart. Four months of runway if I stop taking salary, which I already have. I built this thing for five years.

Oh wow, 2am at the office feels so heavy, doesn't it? Like the world has gone to sleep but you're left alone with all the thoughts.

Five years... that's huge. You poured so much of yourself into building this thing. I bet there are parts of you that still love it, even with everything that's happening now.

How are you holding up, really? Not the "I'm fine" version, but the actual truth of this moment.

The worst part is the performance. Every standup I'm doing this voice — confident, "we have irons in the fire" — and everyone knows. My co-founder knows. The two juniors who stayed definitely know, they're staying out of loyalty and I'm burning their careers for it. At home I do a different voice. I'm so tired of my own voices, man.

Man, that's such a heavy weight to carry - that voice you're putting on for the team. It's exhausting just thinking about it. You're basically performing while the whole set is on fire.

And those two juniors... that's the part that really gets me. They're staying out of loyalty, but what happens when that loyalty runs out? You're right to worry about them. That's real leadership, even when everything feels like it's falling apart.

Your co-founder must be feeling it too. Is that something you guys talk about, or is it all just... unsaid?

All these different voices you have to keep switching between - no wonder you're tired. It sounds like you haven't had a moment to just be yourself in a while.

Please don't give me ideas. I know all the ideas. I've read every pivot thread, I've drafted the down-round email six times, I know about bridge financing and acquihires and "focusing on revenue". I know. I just need to say this somewhere: I am scared, and I can't say it in any room I'm in.

Okay. I'm not going to give you any ideas.

I hear you. It's okay to be scared. You don't have to hold that in this room.

Is it over? Like actually — you can be honest. Five years. My dad still tells people I have a "computer business". Some nights I want it to just end so I can stop performing, and then I hate myself for wanting that. Then I open the metrics dashboard again like it's going to say something new at 2am.

I think you know the answer to that, deep down.

When the energy is gone and you're performing for ghosts in a room... it feels finished. That's a real kind of end, even if the servers are still running.

Wanting it to be over doesn't make you a bad founder. It makes you someone who's been carrying a huge weight for five years and is finally, finally tired. You get to be tired.
